concepts.learning_objective: Distinguish between direct and indirect elections and identify offices filled by each in India.
Explain how regular, periodic and competitive elections keep representatives accountable to the people.
State the meaning and origin of the term psephology.
Explain how the First-Past-The-Post system decides the winner in a constituency.
Compare the majority (two-round) system and proportional representation with FPTP.
Apply the quota rule of the single transferable vote used for the Rajya Sabha, Vidhan Parishad, President and Vice President.

topics.title: The laws and the Delimitation Commission

concepts.learning_objective: Distinguish between the subjects covered by the Representation of the People Acts of 1950 and 1951.
Identify electoral offences and corrupt practices listed in the RPA, 1951.
Explain the purpose of delimitation in ensuring equal representation.
Describe the ECI as an autonomous, permanent constitutional body and the elections it conducts.
Explain how the ECI prepares electoral rolls and why it conducts the Special Intensive Revision.
Describe the ECI's functions of scheduling elections, registering parties and allotting symbols.

topics.title: Free, fair and inclusive elections: no voter to be left behind

concepts.learning_objective: Identify ECI measures that help senior citizens, PwDs and service voters cast their votes.
Match ECI digital applications such as cVIGIL, Suvidha and Saksham to their uses.
Evaluate why fairness, inclusion and trust are needed for elections to have democratic value.
Describe the roles political parties play in a multi-party democracy.
Explain defection and the provisions of the Anti-Defection Law of 1985.
Apply the ECI criteria for recognising national and state parties.

topics.title: Challenges to free and fair elections

concepts.learning_objective: Identify challenges such as misinformation, fake news and intimidation and analyse their effect on democracy.
Explain safeguards such as the Model Code of Conduct, EVMs and VVPAT.
